Article Title: 'If pardoned for one murder, I'd shoot Gyanesh': VIP chief targets CEC over SIR row
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: "If I were pardoned for one murder, the first person I would shoot is Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar!" former Bihar minister and Vikassheel Insaan Party (VIP) chief Mukesh Sahani said on Thursday amid the ongoing row over the functioning of the Election Commission Speaking to reporters, Sahani accused the Election Commission of acting at the BJP's behest and warned that those involved could face jail if the opposition came to power in 2029."The Election Commission has turned into an arm of the BJP. And I want to say to Gyanesh Kumar: times do not stay the same forever. Have some shame - you are playing with the nation's Constitution! If I were pardoned for one murder, the first person I would shoot is Gyanesh! But what can we do? We are law-abiding citizens who respect the Constitution," Sahani said."In the times ahead, they will not go scot-free. In 2029, a government will be formed in the country under the leadership of Rahul Gandhi ji, and Gyanesh Kumar will be the very first person sent to prison. Everyone who colluded with him will also go to jail; no one will be spared. If he passes away before that, that is another matter. But if they remain alive, they will be put behind bars - there are no ifs or buts about it. Nobody will be able to protect him, not even Modi ji.In fact, Modi ji might also end up in jail!" he claimed.Sahani's remarks come after an Indian Express report flagged differences within the poll panel over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. According to the report, Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi formally objected at least 14 times over 10 months to decisions and orders issued in connection with electoral-roll procedures.The Election Commission, meanwhile, said the reported queries and observations by its members were part of its normal internal functioning. The poll panel said written notes, technical suggestions and internal checks were standard practices aimed at ensuring legal compliance and safeguarding voter rights.The ECI also maintained that all its official decisions, including those concerning SIR, had full legal sanction and that the Commission's final decisions were unanimous.The report triggered sharp reactions from Opposition parties, with several leaders demanding greater scrutiny of the Election Commission's decision-making process and questioning Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's functioning.The BJP, meanwhile, defended the poll panel and said internal deliberations were part of democratic functioning.
Article Summary: Mukesh Sahani accuses the Election Commission of acting at the BJP's behest. Former Bihar minister warns those involved could face jail if the opposition comes to power in 2029. Indian Express report flagged differences within the poll panel over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.

Article Title: Gyanesh Kumar should be criminally prosecuted for 'treason': Priyanka Gandhi on SIR row
Article Text:
Cong MP Priyanka Gandhi targets EC over SIR, alleges 'voter roll tampering'.

'Electoral process completely tainted': Cong

'Justice will be served': Rahul

'All actions have been in accordance': EC

'All three Commissioners were unanimous': BJP

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Congress MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra on Thursday slammed the Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, alleging that he should be "criminally prosecuted" if found responsible for "tampering with electoral rolls and deleting voters' names. "Her remarks came a day after The Indian Express published a report claiming that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had formally raised objections at least 14 times over 10 months to decisions and orders related to the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.Speaking to reporters in Wayanad, Kerala, Priyanka Gandhi said, "Anybody who plays around with the process, the democratic process of our elections is committing treason against this nation. That is our very clear stand. I do not think anybody in that position should have legal protection in the way that he has. The Chief Election Commissioner has. If they have done illegal acts because tampering with the voters' rolls, deleting, I believe, 13 crore voters is a criminal act against democracy, against the Constitution and against the nation. ""Since criminal acts fall under a particular law, and people are usually tried and prosecuted for doing those criminal acts, I do not see why the Election Commissioner has to have any protection against it," the Congress MP said."If he has done an illegal act, he has been fully aware that this is happening under his nose. His colleagues have brought it to his attention. He has ignored it and intentionally allowed an unfair election to take place. He should be criminally prosecuted just like any other criminal, and he should be tried for treason. This is my very clear stand," she added.Earlier on Wednesday, Priyanka Gandhi had also called the issue "an extremely serious" one for democracy."This is an extremely serious issue for our democracy. If there are no elections, then where is democracy? If elections are unfair and rigged in any manner, then the Election Commission is assisting in that. If the Election Commissioner is not only aware of it but also allowing it to happen, then it is a very serious assault on democracy. It is an act of treason," she said.Congress leader Jairam Ramesh also launched a fresh attack on Gyanesh Kumar , alleging irregularities in the ECINet software and the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.Ramesh said a series of reports had raised serious questions over the functioning of the poll panel and alleged that the electoral process had been "completely compromised and tainted".He said, "Yesterday, sensational revelations in a major national daily brought to light that the CEC has completely undermined the integrity, reliability, and competence of the Election Commission. This morning, another report in this series has emerged."Ramesh alleged that Goa's chief electoral officer (CEO) wrote to the ECI eight times in seven days seeking the reinstatement of valid voters whose names had been removed by the ECINet software. He said Electoral Registration Officers (EROs) had confirmed that the voters were valid, but their emails were ignored and the names were removed.He also stated that the process for adding new voters through Form 6 had been made more difficult and claimed that Gen Z was being "deliberately targeted" to exclude young voters from electoral rolls.Ramesh said the latest allegations reinforced what leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha, Rahul Gandhi had been saying for nearly two years, referring to the results of the Haryana and Maharashtra assembly elections."The electoral process has been completely compromised and tainted. This is the implementation of the Method of Disenfranchising Indians (MODI) by Gyanesh Kumar," Ramesh said.He also called for the CEC's resignation, saying, "If there is even a shred of decency and ethics left in CEC Gyanesh Kumar, his first step should be to immediately resign from his position. After that, the Prime Minister and Home Minister will be held accountable for their nefarious designs."Congress leader Rahul Gandhi also took to X, stating that, "The enemies of the Constitution have been exposed. Justice will be served."Earlier on Wednesday, Rahul described "vote chori" as a "crime against the Indian people" and an attack on the Constitution.In a post on X, Rahul Gandhi said, "Vote chori is a crime against the Indian people and a direct attack on our constitution. The BJP, RSS and EC who organised it have committed an act of treason. Justice will be served."In a video, he also addressed the Election Commission and election officials, saying, "I am clearly telling the Election Commission and election officers: What you are doing is wrong. This is treason; it is against the nation. Do not forget this. The time will come! We will catch you! You will not be spared."According to the media report, Election Commissioners Sandhu and Joshi had objected at least 14 times to decisions taken in the Commission's name without their knowledge or approval. The reported objections covered issues including voter registration and deletion, changes to Form 6 and the handling of the electoral-roll database.The ECI rejected the suggestion that the reported objections amounted to a division within the Commission. ECI officials said all decisions, including those related to SIR, were taken unanimously with the approval of all three commissioners.In a statement, the poll panel said, "The ECI is a constitutional body that functions under the strict mandate of Article 324 of the Constitution, statutory rules and established institutional conventions. The Commission operates as a multi-member constitutional body. Written notes, observations, technical suggestions and internal checks-and-balances are standard, ongoing practices designed to ensure complete transparency, legal compliance and operational rigour. All actions of ECI have been in accordance with laws and instructions of the Commission. All official orders, decisions and administrative directions issued by the Commission carry full legal sanctions and follow established statutory procedures."The Commission further said, "Any operational queries or inputs raised by Commission members during draft stages are part of standard administrative practice aimed at safeguarding voter rights. The suggestions given by the Commissioners were for further improving the electoral processes," adding that differing views and observations were a normal part of institutional deliberations.BJP national spokesperson and MP Sambit Patra earlier defended the functioning of the Election Commission, saying discussions among the three commissioners were part of the democratic process."Look at the situation: if the three Election Commissioners do not communicate with each other, if there is no exchange of views or consultation, and they simply agree to everything, then the opposition parties claim it is a dictatorship. They say this government appointed these three commissioners; they just say yes. Now, there have been 14 instances of correspondence among the three of them, official deliberations, as far as we gather from the media. It is not as if the Bharatiya Janata Party goes and reads these letters; rather, reports in the media indicate that official deliberations took place among the three, which is a sign of a healthy democracy," he said."I would say that today, all the opposition parties have fallen into a trap, the trap of claiming that the Election Commission and the government were acting dictatorially. On the contrary, I would say this is pure democracy.Deliberations are taking place, and the Election Commission has stated very clearly in the very first paragraph of its document that, following all official democratic deliberations, the final outcome, the Special Intensive Revision (SIR), was achieved with unanimity," Patra said."In other words, all three Commissioners were unanimous; there was no difference of opinion or dissent among them," he added.Meanwhile, ECI sources maintained that all decisions taken by the poll panel, including those related to SIR, were unanimous and had the approval of both Election Commissioners and the Chief Election Commissioner.
Article Summary: Congress leader Jairam Ramesh also launched a fresh attack on Gyanesh Kumar, alleging irregularities in the ECINet software and the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. He said a series of reports had raised serious questions over the functioning of the poll panel and alleged that the electoral process had been "completely compromised"

Article Title: Tamil Nadu Pocso case: Businessman Veeramani, aide arrested; what we know so far
Article Text:
Child rape: Granite baron Veeramani’s premises raided

What is the Veeramani case?

Case takes political turn

NEW DELHI: The Central Crime Branch (CCB) has arrested Ganesan, a longtime aide of granite businessman and Gem Granites chief Veeramani, in connection with a POCSO case involving the alleged sexual abuse of minor girls.Ganesan is the fourth accused arrested in the case. Police said he had worked with Veeramani’s Gem Granites for 23 years and is currently employed with Balaji Global Enterprises.According to investigators, Ganesan had video clips on his mobile phone that purportedly showed Veeramani in an obscene act involving a minor girl. Police said he did not inform the authorities about the videos.The CCB is now investigating how Ganesan came to possess the clips and why he allegedly kept them without alerting police. Investigators are also examining his mobile phone to determine whether any data was deleted.Veeramani was arrested on August 29 along with two alleged accomplices after the Anti-Vice Squad (AVS) registered a case over the alleged rape of minor girls. The three accused were subsequently remanded in Puzhal Central Prison.Police said the case came to light after a USB drive containing a video clip purportedly showing Veeramani sexually assaulting a juvenile girl was recovered.Investigators identified the survivor and established that she was a minor when the alleged offence took place in 2019.The video was also examined as part of the investigation into the allegations against Veeramani.The investigation has also expanded to suspected financial transactions allegedly made to influence the earlier probe, police said.Investigators are examining bank transactions and the possible involvement of intermediaries in the movement of funds.The ruling TVK on Wednesday demanded that DMK president MK Stalin explain how the POCSO case involving Veeramani was handled when the DMK was in power, alleging that the investigation was allowed to weaken and questioning why a final report was filed.The TVK alleged that the case had been “buried”. The party also questioned former law minister S. Regupathy over his handling of video footage submitted in connection with the case.“Under whose pressure did the then Law Minister Regupathy allow the investigation to be weakened? What was the reason?” the TVK asked.The party also sought an explanation for the filing of the final report, alleging that it was submitted without a proper investigation.Chennai Central Crime Branch police have issued summons to Assistant Commissioner Yasmin and Anti-Vice Squad inspectors Mahesh Kumar and Rajalakshmi in connection with the sexual assault case against industrialist Veeramani.The three officials, who had earlier investigated and closed the case, have been asked to appear in person for an inquiry and provide their explanations, Chennai Police said.
Article Summary: Ganesan is the fourth accused arrested in the case. Ganesan had video clips on his mobile phone that purportedly showed Veeramani in an obscene act involving a minor girl. Police said he did not inform the authorities about the videos. The investigation has also expanded to suspected financial transactions allegedly made to influence the earlier probe.

Congress leader Rahul Gandhi spoke to the parents of deceased IIT Bombay student Sahil Wakode and assured them of all possible help in their fight to seek justice for their son, party sources said told PTI on Thrusday.Rahul Gandhi made a video call to Ravindra and Sonali Wakode while they were travelling to Mumbai from Washim district, the sources told PTI. During the nearly 17 minute call, Gandhi told the couple that he was with them and assured them of all help.Indian Youth Congress president Uday Bhanu Chib and Maharashtra unit chief Shivraj More were also present with Sahil’s parents during the call.The conversation comes amid growing protests and demands for an independent probe into Sahil’s death. His parents have alleged that their son faced caste based discrimination and mental harassment at IIT Bombay and have sought action against those they hold responsible.Sahil, a second year BTech student at IIT Bombay, was found hanging in his hostel room on the evening of September 18. His death occurred hours after he was allegedly caught using a mobile phone to access ChatGPT during a mid semester examination.The examination incident became a key focus of the case after Sahil was allegedly stopped by a professor and taken out of the examination hall.CCTV footage from the hall, aired by some television channels on Wednesday, reportedly shows Sahil’s movements before the professor approaches him and leads him away.The Mumbai Police Crime Branch is investigating the death. An FIR has been registered alleging abetment to suicide on grounds of caste discrimination. Faculty member Suryanarayan Doolla, who has been named in the FIR, has been sent on leave to facilitate an impartial investigation.IIT Bombay has maintained that its SC/ST cell had not received a complaint from Sahil before his death. The institute has also constituted a 10 member committee to examine the circumstances surrounding the incident.Sahil’s parents have announced that they will begin an indefinite hunger strike outside the IIT Bombay gate from 11 am on Thursday. Their demands include a thorough investigation into the circumstances preceding their son’s death and action based on the findings of the probe.
Article Summary: Sahil Wakode, a second year BTech student at IIT Bombay, was found hanging in his hostel room on the evening of September 18. His death occurred hours after he was allegedly caught using a mobile phone to access ChatGPT during a mid semester examination. An FIR has been registered alleging abetment to suicide on grounds of caste discrimination.

Canadian PM Mark Carney has said his counterpart, Narendra Modi, could travel to Canada in Dec, while citing good progress in negotiations for a trade agreement.He said the two sides were hoping to wrap up trade talks by Dec and he was looking forward to hosting Modi.Modi is expected to club his Canada visit to sign the trade agreement with his trip to Florida for the G20 summit. It is an exceptionally important relationship on many, many levels - people-to-people levels, security levels, and also trade and economic," Carney said Tuesday on the sidelines of the UNGA high-level session.He said Modi and he had committed at the G20 last year to "look to conclude negotiations by the G20 this year".US President Donald Trump will host the G20 Summit from Dec 14-15 at Trump National Doral Miami resort in Doral, Florida.Carney said with the G20 Summit slated to be held in Dec, "I believe that India just confirmed that the PM will be visiting Canada around that time. The precise date isn't out, but I very much look forward to hosting him".Modi last visited Canada to attend the G7 Summit in June 2025 at Carney's invitation.

NEW DELHI: US ambassador to India Sergio Gor made a rare appearance at a Chinese event here on Wednesday, as White House rolled out a red carpet for President Xi Jinping for a potentially landmark visit.Gor joined Chinese ambassador Xu Feihong for a reception hosted by the latter at a 5-star hotel to celebrate the 77th anniversary of the founding of People's Republic of China. India's commerce secretary, Rajesh Aggarwal, was the chief guest. Russian ambassador Denis Alipov was also present.Unlike on such occasions in recent years, the anniversary saw a heavy presence of top Western diplomats, including the envoys of Germany, Canada and Netherlands.Xu reiterated Beijing's position that India and China were partners, not rivals. The ambassador said that as two ancient civilisations, China and India had sufficient political and historical wisdom to handle differences properly."We stay committed to striving for a dual-track approach to bilateral relations and border issues with each reinforcing the other and maintaining peace and tranquillity in the border areas so as to ensure bilateral relations advance on the right track," said Xu, adding, "It would be mutually beneficial for us to strengthen friendly exchanges and win-win cooperation, enhance public support for our bilateral ties, and assist each other's develo-pment and revitalisation. "

Article Title: India's proposal under consideration for safe Black Sea shipping, Zelenskyy says
Article Text:
File photo: Prime Minister Narendra Modi during a meeting with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy (Picture credit: PTI)

India has been pushing for dialogue

Black Sea shipping remains key concern

Russia yet to back proposals

India has emerged as one of the countries whose proposals are being considered for restoring safe commercial shipping in the Black Sea, with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy saying Egypt, India and Turkey have outlined options for a maritime truce between Russia and Ukraine.Speaking to leaders at the United Nations on Wednesday, Zelenskyy said Ukraine was ready to support a maritime truce based on the proposals and that Russia now needed to respond.“We are waiting for Russia's response. Ukraine is ready ... to ensure safe shipping and food security in the Black Sea if Russia is ready to take real steps towards de-escalation too. We have to start somewhere,” Zelenskyy said.The remarks came at Ukraine's Crimean Platform summit on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly, ahead of a UN Security Council meeting on Russia's war in Ukraine.The reference to India's role comes amid New Delhi's efforts to remain engaged with both Moscow and Kyiv and encourage an end to the conflict.External affairs minister S Jaishankar said earlier this month that India had been in continuous touch with both Ukraine and Russia and was exploring ideas that could contribute to mitigating and eventually ending the war.“What we are trying to do is to see if there are ideas and suggestions which can be developed in some way in which they will contribute to the mitigation, ideally, the cessation of the conflict,” Jaishankar said during his visit to Warsaw.Jaishankar has also said India's position is that the conflict should end through dialogue and diplomacy.During his visit to Kyiv earlier this month, he met Zelenskyy and Ukrainian foreign minister Andrii Sybiha, with discussions including possible approaches to ending the conflict.“If India can be of any help, in any manner, we are there,” Jaishankar said in Kyiv.According to Reuters, Zelenskyy said Egypt, India and Turkey had proposed options to restore safe navigation for merchant vessels in the Black Sea, where cargo movements have been severely disrupted by attacks on ships and port infrastructure by both sides.Ukraine has been seeking ceasefires covering attacks on energy infrastructure as well as shipping in the Black Sea. Kyiv has also expressed concern that Russia could target power and heating facilities with missiles and drones during the winter.The disruption has also affected countries dependent on grain supplies from the Black Sea region. Reuters reported that wheat importers in Asia, the Middle East and Africa have faced difficulties securing supplies, while global wheat prices have risen.Zelenskyy said Ukraine was ready to ensure safe shipping and food security if Russia was prepared to take steps towards de-escalation.US secretary of state Marco Rubio said after meeting Russian foreign minister Sergei Lavrov on Wednesday that both Russia and Ukraine had expressed interest in a limited ceasefire involving grain and energy.The Kremlin has not publicly backed the proposals.Ahead of the Rubio-Lavrov meeting, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said there were currently no grounds for broader peace talks, while maintaining that Russia remained open to negotiations.“For now, there are no prerequisites for moving on to a peaceful negotiating track, although we, as the Russian side, remain open to peace talks,” Peskov said.Zelenskyy also said he was ready to meet Russian President Vladimir Putin at a trilateral meeting with US President Donald Trump.The latest developments come as India continues its diplomatic engagement with both sides.Jaishankar met US secretary of state Marco Rubio on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly on Wednesday and discussed the Ukraine situation, as well as India's concerns over the US Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act.
Article Summary: India has emerged as one of the countries whose proposals are being considered for restoring safe commercial shipping in the Black Sea. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Egypt, India and Turkey have outlined options for a maritime truce between Russia and Ukraine. Russia yet to back proposals.

Article Title: 'Deliberations sign of pure democracy': BJP reacts to EC 'SIR split' row, targets Congress
Article Text:
He said opposition parties had questioned the functioning of the three election commissioners both when they appeared to agree and now when correspondence between them has emerged.

Patra targets opposition

NEW DELHI: The BJP on Wednesday defended the election commission over the row surrounding an alleged split among the poll panel's commissioners, with party MP Sambit Patra saying that internal deliberations between the three election commissioners were a sign of a healthy democracy. He also accused the Congress of attacking constitutional institutions after failing to win elections.Addressing a press conference, Patra referred to the EC's press note and said correspondence among the three election commissioners had taken place on 14 occasions."I am not here to hold a press conference on behalf of the Election Commission. I have brought the press note issued by the EC, and I have read it. I hope you have also read it," he said.Patra said the correspondence showed that the commissioners had formally exchanged views and consulted one another.He added, "But now there has been correspondence among the three commissioners on 14 occasions. This is official deliberation among the three election commissioners. What do we gather from this? The BJP did not go and plant a story in the media saying that there had been official deliberations among the three commissioners.Such deliberations are actually a sign of a healthy democracy..."Patra also hit out at opposition parties over their criticism of the EC, accusing them of attacking constitutional institutions.He said opposition parties had questioned the functioning of the three election commissioners both when they appeared to agree and now when correspondence between them has emerged."If the three election commissioners who conduct elections in the country do not communicate with each other, do not exchange views or consult one another, and simply keep agreeing with each other, then the Opposition parties say, 'This is a dictatorship.'""They say, 'This government appointed all three of them, and they simply keep saying yes to everything. They are all supporters of Modi.'"Patra said the opposition had also used the term "Godi media" for sections of the media and was now making similar allegations against the poll panel."You say the same thing about the media, calling it 'Godi media', and now you say these three commissioners are also 'Godi' people."Patra linked the latest controversy to what he described as a broader Congress campaign against constitutional institutions."You know how, since 2014, when the Modi government came to power, opposition parties have been falling one after another. They did not fall on a battlefield, but in the democratic arena, as their existence came under threat because they were not chosen by the people," he said.He claimed the Congress had subsequently turned its focus to institutions after finding itself unable to win elections.He added, "After that, particularly the Congress party realised that it could not win elections, and so the biggest weapon in its hands was to 'kill the institutions of the country'. It began attacking our constitutional institutions and trying to defame them."Patra said the criticism of the EC was part of the same campaign, "In the same context and as part of the same campaign, several parties have held press conferences today regarding the Election Commission."
Article Summary: BJP MP Sambit Patra says internal deliberations between the three election commissioners were a sign of a healthy democracy. He also accused the Congress of attacking constitutional institutions after failing to win elections. Patra said the opposition had also used the term "Godi media" for sections of the media and was making similar allegations against the poll panel.

Article Title: EC 'dissent' row: Opposition seeks CEC's arrest, fresh polls in states; BJP lauds 'pure democracy' - top developments
Article Text:
SIR row explodes into political confrontation as Opposition demands action against CEC

Opposition demands CEC's removal, arrest

Fresh polls demanded in Bihar, West Bengal

Akhilesh, Omar question EC functioning

BJP says EC differences show ‘pure democracy’

EC says all decisions were unanimous

NEW DELHI: The reported objections raised by two Election Commissioners to decisions linked to the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls triggered a major political confrontation on Wednesday, with opposition parties demanding action against chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, an immediate halt to the SIR exercise and fresh elections in states where polls have already been held.The ruling BJP, however, defended the Election Commission, saying differences expressed by Election Commissioners during internal deliberations showed that the poll panel was functioning democratically rather than under a “dictatorial” system.The political row followed a media report which said Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had raised objections at least 14 times over 10 months to decisions and orders related to the SIR process and electoral rolls.The Election Commission has rejected the suggestion that the reported objections indicated a breakdown in its functioning.It said differing views and observations were a normal part of institutional deliberations and maintained that its decisions, including those concerning SIR, had been taken unanimously.Opposition parties, which have been criticising the EC over the SIR exercise, seized on the report to renew their demands for action against Gyanesh Kumar.Congress leader Rahul Gandhi reiterated his “vote chori” allegation against the Election Commission, describing it as “a crime against the people of India” and an attack on the Constitution.“The BJP, RSS and EC who organised it have committed an act of treason. Justice will be served,” Rae Bareli MP said.Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge said 73 Opposition Rajya Sabha MPs had submitted a fresh notice on April 24, seeking Kumar's removal.He questioned whether the Rajya Sabha chairman would decide on the pending notice since the Monsoon Session of Parliament had not yet been prorogued.Shiv Sena (UBT) chief Uddhav Thackeray and AAP national convenor Arvind Kejriwal went further, demanding that Kumar be removed and arrested.“Gyanesh Kumar should be immediately sacked and jailed,” Thackeray said.He also demanded that the last elections in Maharashtra, West Bengal and Tamil Nadu be nullified and fresh polls held in the three states using ballot papers.Kejriwal demanded that the entire SIR exercise be cancelled, all changes made under it be reversed and the voter list from three years ago be restored. He also called for Kumar's arrest and registration of a sedition case against him.TMC MP Derek O'Brien said, “Impeach CEC to save democracy.”Former West Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee also demanded Kumar's arrest and said he had “no moral authority to continue”.“This is such a scandalous story. We had never seen this in our lives. This Election Commissioner must be arrested. He has no moral authority to continue, and the BJP must see that they cannot destroy our Constitution. They cannot demolish democracy,” Banerjee said.The Opposition's demands also extended to fresh elections in states where polls have already taken place.RJD leader and Bihar leader of opposition Tejashwi Yadav demanded fresh elections in Bihar and West Bengal, alleging that the electoral mandates in the two states had been compromised through electoral fraud and institutional manipulation.“The opposition did not lose elections on the ground; the results were orchestrated by PM Modi and Amit Shah. In 2020, we were defeated through manipulation, and the same script was executed in 2025. Voter lists were purged, money was distributed, and counting was manipulated. The electoral outcomes in Bihar and Bengal are fraudulent, and we demand that fresh, transparent elections be held,” he said.Yadav also questioned changes to the rules governing the preservation of voting and counting records, alleging that the period had been reduced from one year to 45 days.He said this could make it difficult for parties to approach courts without access to election-related evidence.DMK president M K Stalin demanded Kumar's resignation and an immediate halt to the SIR exercise. He also sought a fair probe “into everything that transpired within the EC and those responsible should be held accountable”, according to news agency PTI.Stalin alleged that the report had raised doubts about the results of Assembly elections held after the SIR exercise and said his party had consistently opposed the deletion of voters from electoral rolls in the name of SIR.Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav said governments formed during a period when the Election Commission was not functioning impartially were “unconstitutional”.“This means that the governments which have been formed during this period are unconstitutional governments,” Yadav said.He alleged that interference in the poll panel amounted to “trampling” democracy and urged the Supreme Court to take suo motu cognisance of the matter.Jammu and Kashmir chief minister Omar Abdullah said the Centre and the Election Commission needed to take corrective steps to prevent people from losing faith in elections.“Corrective action needs to be taken somewhere. Otherwise, if people lose faith in elections, what remains of a democracy? Elections are the very foundations of a democracy. If people lose faith in elections, why would they even participate in them? I feel the Election Commission and the government of India need to reflect on this,” Abdullah said.He also said the report raised questions about the functioning of the poll panel and referred to his earlier concerns over the electoral process.The BJP rejected the Opposition's allegations and defended the reported differences between the Election Commissioners.Addressing a press conference at the BJP headquarters, party spokesperson Sambit Patra said differing views during official deliberations showed that the poll panel was functioning democratically.“The media reports saying that the election commissioners shared differing views in official deliberations is a reflection of pure democracy,” Patra said.“If there is no communication and exchange of views among the election commissioners who conduct polls, the opposition parties would allege 'dictatorship' and call them 'yes men' of the government,” he said.Patra said the Election Commission's response showed that neither the poll panel nor other constitutional bodies were functioning under a “dictatorial rule”.“This shows that the Election Commission (EC) and all other constitutional bodies are functioning in a democratic manner and upholding the democracy of the country,” he said.Responding to the media report, the Election Commission said written notes, observations, technical suggestions and internal checks and balances were standard practices within a multi-member constitutional body.“The ECI is a constitutional body that functions under the strict mandate of Article 324 of the Constitution, statutory rules and established institutional conventions. The Commission operates as a multi-member constitutional body. Written notes, observations, technical suggestions and internal checks-and-balances are standard, ongoing practices designed to ensure complete transparency, legal compliance and operational rigour,” it said.The commission said all official orders, decisions and administrative directions carried full legal sanction and followed established statutory procedures. It added that operational queries or inputs raised by members during the drafting stage were part of standard administrative practice aimed at safeguarding voter rights and improving electoral processes.The EC further said differing views and observations were a normal part of deliberation before a final decision was taken.“Not only the three Commissioners, but every officer of the Commission is fully authorised to give his suggestions to the Commission for improving the electoral system,” it said.The commission said focusing on specific internal notes and observations over 10 months while overlooking its wider body of approvals, decisions, instructions and initiatives presented only one part of the picture.It said it had taken numerous decisions, issued instructions and introduced around 40 new initiatives and electoral reforms, including electoral-roll revision and SIR across the country.“All these decisions are an outcome of the unanimous decisions of the full Commission in the past one year,” the EC said.The commission also pointed to the conduct of elections in Bihar, Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Puducherry, Assam and West Bengal during the period and said it remained committed to carrying out its constitutional duties.
Article Summary: Opposition parties demand action against chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. They also demand an immediate halt to the SIR exercise and fresh elections in states where polls have already been held. The ruling BJP, however, defended the Election Commission, saying differences expressed by Election Commissioners during internal deliberations showed the poll panel was functioning democratically.

Article Title: Judges appointing judges is a myth, says Justice Datta, points to way in which govt clears collegium picks
Article Text:
Judges appointing judges is a myth, says Justice Datta

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Holding that the collegium system remains the most viable option for safeguarding judicial independence despite its "opacity and imperfections", Justice Dipankar Datta Wednesday said its deficiencies could not justify ushering in executive participation in collegium deliberations. He said judiciary had been relegated to playing second fiddle to the executive in appointments because of the way collegium recommendations were cleared by govt.Referring to govt's argument that the judiciary had an exclusive say in judges' appointments, Datta said "judiciary cannot always be at the receiving end" and devoted six pages to the issue, saying "relevant observations in response need to be made, lest the silence be misunderstood as a tacit acceptance by the court of such unworthy criticism in circulation".Datta said the executive wielded decisive control and held the reins over appointments at every level. He said it had become fashionable to blame the collegium for every infelicitous choice, conveniently forgetting that aberrations were exceptions and not the norm, and that no system could guarantee infallibility of human choice.The other judge on the bench, Justice S C Sharma said SG Tushar Mehta's submission was "not a criticism of the collegium system or regarding the role of executive in the appointment of judges"."It was a submission to the effect that if the constitution bench has held the presence of outsiders in collegium as violative of doctrine of separation of powers, a similar independence should be read in executive and rules framed under Art 324 be not declared void on the ground that it does not have an outsider in the selection committee or the executive predominates in it," he said.Sharma said the SG had based his argument on the judgment in the National Judicial Appointments Commission case, where a constitution bench held that the presence of even the law minister in the collegium for appointment of SC and HC judges would violate separation of powers. "Building upon the constitutional principle, the submission of the SG was that a corresponding degree of constitutional independence must be recognised for the executive as well as legislature. He submitted that the committee constituted under rules framed under Art 324 deserves to be declared legal though dominated by members of executive," Sharma said.Datta said, "The oft-repeated phrase that 'judges appoint judges' is a myth, which people have been fed by vested interests through motivated narratives. A sweeping generalisation that collegium acts as a law unto itself overlooks the consultative process envisaged under the Constitution, and the intrinsic role of executive - both at Centre and in the states."He added, "It is undeniable that collegium system has occasionally faltered and its functioning has not been free from aberrations. However, vociferous criticism, by itself, does not offer an alternative.While absence of an outsider may invite scrutiny, executive supremacy cannot be the cure. The constitutional quest is not to transfer primacy from one organ to another, but to preserve independence through checks and balances."What is worrying is that the sanctity of a collegium resolution is lost each time the executive implements it selectively, approving majority of those recommended while withholding one. Undeterred by piecemeal approvals and fate of those not cleared by the executive, collegium chooses to proceed, to avoid a head-on conflict with the executive, left with a Hobson's choice to keep the institution running. What it averts is a constitutional crisis; but the larger question is: how long can this state of affairs continue, if selective implementation is allowed to acquire the character of an accepted practice?"
Article Summary: Justice Dipankar Datta said the executive wielded decisive control and held the reins over appointments at every level. He said it had become fashionable to blame the collegium for every infelicitous choice, conveniently forgetting that aberrations were exceptions and not the norm. Datta devoted six pages to the issue, saying "relevant observations in response need to be made"

AMRITSAR: The officiating Jathedar of Akal Takht and Jathedar of Takht Sri Kesgarh Sahib, Giani Kuldip Singh Gargajj, wrote a letter to Pakistan’s Punjab chief minister Maryam Nawaz Sharif, asking for the protection and preservation of Sikh historical heritage sites in Lahore’s Walled City, particularly Lal Khooh, Kattari Chandu, associated with the martyrdom of Sri Guru Arjan Dev Ji.In his letter, addressed to the Punjab Chief Minister, copied to Provincial Minister and Pakistan Sikh Gurdwara Parbandhak Committee president Ramesh Singh Arora, the Jathedar asked that the Pakistan Punjab Government to immediately conduct an inquiry into the present status of Lal Khooh, Kattari Chandu in Lahore.“If any construction or alteration work is underway at the site, stop it immediately until the inquiry is completed”, writes Giani Gargajj.He also asked to get the historical and heritage significance of the site examined by experts from the Walled City of Lahore Authority, Archaeology Department and other concerned departments and suggested to include Sikh history experts and representatives of the Pakistan Sikh Gurdwara Parbandhak Committee in the inquiry process.If the historical significance of the site is established, initiate necessary action to have it legally protected as a heritage site.He suggested to conduct a comprehensive heritage survey of all major sites associated with Sikh history in Lahore’s Walled City, documenting their present condition, historical significance, ownership and legal status.In the letter, he wrote that the issue concerning Lal Khooh, Kattari Chandu, in Lahore’s Walled City had been brought to the attention of Sri Akal Takht Sahib by the Sikh sangat. He said there are concerns regarding construction-related activity around the site, which was a matter of serious concern for Sikhs.However, rather than relying on assumptions, he called for an official fact-finding inquiry into the matter.At the same time, he clarified that the purpose of the communication was not to level allegations against any government, institution or individual, but to draw attention to Lahore’s shared historical heritage and the important chapters of Sikh history associated with the city.
Article Summary: Giani Kuldip Singh Gargajj wrote a letter to Pakistan’s Punjab chief minister Maryam Nawaz Sharif. He asked for the protection and preservation of Sikh historical heritage sites in Lahore's Walled City, particularly Lal Khooh, Kattari Chandu, associated with Sri Guru Arjan Dev Ji.

Article Title: Israeli soldier accused of Gaza war crimes leaves India after complaint by Palestinian group: Report
Article Text:
The soldier, whose identity has not been made public, left India in mid-September.

Second Israeli soldier to leave India after complaint

An Israeli soldier accused of alleged war crimes in Gaza has left India weeks after the Hind Rajab Foundation (HRF), a Palestinian rights group, filed a criminal complaint against him, according to a report by Middle East Eye.The soldier, whose identity has not been made public, left India in mid-September, a lawyer familiar with the case told Middle East Eye. It remains unclear whether the complaint influenced his departure or whether he left after completing his holiday.The development comes amid renewed calls for countries to uphold international law. External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar, speaking on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly in New York on Monday, said multilateralism works best when international law, rules and norms are "scrupulously observed".The latest case marks the second incident this year in which the Hind Rajab Foundation (HRF) has identified an Israeli soldier travelling in India and filed a complaint against him.In June, the Brussels-based organisation approached Indian authorities seeking the arrest of Eitan Gilboa, an Israeli military reservist who was vacationing in Himachal Pradesh. HRF accused Gilboa, who was identified as a member of the Israeli military's 271st Combat Engineering Battalion, of involvement in the demolition of civilian buildings in Khan Younis and Rafah.According to reports, HRF submitted material, including geolocated videos, social media posts and chain-of-command documentation to Indian authorities. Gilboa was subsequently traced by pro-Palestinian activists to locations including Old Manali and Gondla in Himachal Pradesh before leaving India.The latest case has followed a similar sequence, with HRF identifying an Israeli soldier through publicly available information, filing a complaint with Indian authorities and the individual subsequently leaving the country.India has long been a popular destination for young Israelis after their mandatory military service. Many undertake an extended post-service trip, commonly known as "tiul gadol", which can last several months.The trend has also contributed to the informal "Hummus Trail" followed by Israeli travellers across several Indian destinations, including Kasol, Dharamkot, Goa, Hampi, Gokarna, Kodaikanal, Rishikesh, Varanasi and Pushkar.Tourism has also featured in India-Israel bilateral cooperation. In February 2026, Israel allocated 4 million shekels for initiatives aimed at strengthening tourism ties with India.The HRF has increasingly sought to pursue legal complaints against Israeli military personnel over alleged conduct during Israel's military campaign in Gaza. The organisation's complaints have also brought attention to the presence of former and serving Israeli military personnel travelling in countries including India.Israel launched its military campaign in Gaza following the Hamas-led attacks on southern Israel on October 7, 2023.
Article Summary: Second Israeli soldier to leave India after complaint by Palestinian rights group. Soldier, whose identity has not been made public, left India in mid- September. It remains unclear whether the complaint influenced his departure or whether he left after completing his holiday. Development comes amid renewed calls for countries to uphold international law.

NEW DELHI: Samajwadi Party president Akhilesh Yadav on Wednesday questioned the functioning of the Election Commission, saying governments formed during a period when the poll panel was not acting impartially were “unconstitutional”.Addressing a press conference in Lucknow, Yadav referred to a report that said Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had recorded objections 14 times over 10 months to decisions and orders related to the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) process and electoral roll procedures.Yadav said the Election Commission was regarded as an impartial institution and was expected to strengthen democracy. He questioned “on whose behalf” the poll panel was functioning if its own members were raising objections to its decisions.“This is dangerous for our democracy. This is an attempt to weaken our democracy,” he said.The SP chief said the Election Commission was a constitutional body and questioned who was “playing with” such an institution for the purpose of remaining in government.“What can you imagine now? Would the Election Commission have been fair? Would it have been impartial?” he asked.Yadav said the reported objections from within the poll panel raised questions about the functioning of an institution whose basic expectation was impartiality.“This means that the governments which have been formed during this period are unconstitutional governments,” he said, alleging that democracy had been “trampled upon”.In an earlier post on X, Yadav described the reported objections by the two Election Commissioners as “extremely serious news”.“It is extremely serious news that in the last 10 months, two Election Commissioners have recorded their objections 14 times to the wrong decisions of the Election Commission,” he said.“Making democracy a victim by becoming puppets of some people in power is a grave constitutional crime. It is no less than a conspiracy to destroy democracy,” Yadav said, urging the Supreme Court to take suo motu cognisance of the matter.Yadav also alleged that voters supporting the Samajwadi Party had been “systematically deleted” from electoral rolls and claimed no corrective action was taken after the issue was brought to the Election Commission's notice.“The Election Commission claims it will strengthen democracy. When such things are happening within the Election Commission itself, where can one place their trust? In the span of 10 months, various officials have written letters 14 times. Samajwadi Party voters were systematically deleted from the Election Commission's voters list. We brought this to the notice of the Election Commission, but no action was taken against anyone. Rampant malpractice was committed on a massive scale in the by-elections,” Yadav said.The Election Commission, however, said all its decisions, including those related to SIR, were taken unanimously with the approval of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and the two other Election Commissioners.Responding to the report, the EC said written notes, observations, technical suggestions and internal checks were standard practices within a multi-member constitutional body. It said all official orders and decisions carried full legal sanction and followed established statutory procedures.The commission said differing views were part of institutional deliberations before a final decision was taken. It also said it had introduced around 40 new initiatives and undertaken electoral reforms, including electoral-roll revision and SIR.Yadav also accused the BJP government in Uttar Pradesh of arbitrary governance.“The government is acting arbitrarily. It is dismantling every system. Those who believe in demolition and destruction—whether it comes to the law or the Constitution—simply do not care about anything. This government is trampling upon everyone’s dignity and self-respect,” he said.On Ayodhya , Yadav said the SP had never opposed construction of the Ram Temple but accused the BJP of displacing local residents through demolition drives.“We have never wanted to be an obstacle in the development of the Lord Shri Ram Temple in Ayodhya, nor will we ever be in the future. We will develop a far better city of Ayodhya than they ever could.They are snatching away the rights of the poor,” he said.The Election Commission controversy has also drawn criticism from other Opposition parties, with Congress MP Rahul Gandhi questioning the poll panel and CEC Gyanesh Kumar over alleged “vote chori”.Opposition parties had earlier moved motions seeking the removal of Gyanesh Kumar.
Article Summary: Samajwadi Party president Akhilesh Yadav questions the functioning of the Election Commission. In recent months, the Commission has taken numerous decisions, issued instructions, introduced around 40 new initiatives and undertaken many electoral reforms including the conduct of electoral roll revision (including SIR) across the country.All these decisions are an outcome of the unanimous decisions of the full Commission in the past one year,” the commission stated.The statement reiterated that EC, a constitutional body functioning under the strict mandate of Article 324 of the Constitution, statutory roles and established institutional conventions, operates as a multi-member constitutional body, "Written notes, observations, technical suggestions and internal checks-and-balances are standard, ongoing practices designed to ensure complete transparency, legal compliance and operational rigour,” it noted.The commission said all official orders, decisions and administrative directions issued by the Commission carry full legal sanction and follow established statutory procedures under The Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act, 2023."The Commission has recently successfully conducted major elections of Bihar, Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Puducherry, Assam and West Bengal and election-related exercises during this period. Statutory authorities, including EROs and district election officers (DEOs), function as per statutory powers for registration and deletion under law,” said EC.The poll body signed off saying that it “remains fully committed to executing its constitutional duties with complete integrity, recognizing its vital role in advancing our democracy”.
Article Summary: Election Commission concedes that “operational queries or inputs” were raised by election commissioners S S Sandhu and Vivek Joshi on matters including the special intensive revision (SIR) exercise. Article Title: 'Inappropriate to ask': Years before Sahil Wakode's death, IIT-Bombay professor warned students against caste discrimination
Article Text:
Prof Suryanarayana Doolla (L), CCTV captures Sahil Wakode looking at phone during exam.

Mail sent by Prof Doolla

An Apology

Sahil Wakode’s death

Poll Vote & Share your view Do you feel that online platforms like WhatsApp and Facebook should be monitored for discriminatory messages? Absolutely, it's necessary. No, it's an invasion of privacy. 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Probe into allegations





MUMBAI: A 2024 email sent by IIT Bombay professor Suryanarayana Doolla, who was then the institute’s Dean of Student Affairs, has resurfaced amid allegations of caste discrimination made by the family of student Sahil Wakode, who died by suicide last week.In the email, prof Doolla cautioned students against asking fellow students about their admission categories, JEE (Advanced) ranks or GATE scores, saying such questions could reveal their caste or whether they belonged to a reserved category.The email said IIT Bombay aimed to promote an inclusive campus where students interacted with each other irrespective of caste, religion or socio-economic status."IIT Bombay considers it inappropriate to ask a fellow student what birth/admission category they belong to: asking this could lead to conscious or subconscious bias.It is equally inappropriate for any person (students/staff/faculty-members) to ask other students about their JEE (Advanced) ranks/GATE-scores, or any other information that may reveal the caste or other related aspects. While the person asking the question may feel it is innocent, and it may be driven purely by curiosity, asking the question can often have an adverse impact on the other student. Asking could appear like an attempt to find the caste, and may set the stage for discrimination.The message also urged students to build friendships around common interests such as their department, sports, music, films, schools, colleges, villages, cities and hobbies."It is prohibited to exchange/forward any messages, including jokes, that are abusive, hateful, casteist, sexist, exhibit bigotry e.g. based on - religion or sexual orientation, can be construed as harassment or bullying."The email said the prohibition applied to messages shared on WhatsApp, Facebook and email, as well as interactions in person, and warned that violations could lead to severe punishment.The email was circulated during prof Doolla’s tenure as dean. IIT Bombay had also circulated its anti-discrimination guidelines twice during his tenure.The institue on Thursday issued a formal apology over statements made in an earlier communication about the circumstances surrounding the death of student Sahil Ravindra Wakode.Re-sharing a statement originally published on X on September 21, IIT Bombay said it had been premature to release or characterise details about the events leading up to the incident before formal inquiries were completed.“Sharing the earlier post of 21st Sept 2026 again: We apologise for the statements contained in our earlier communication concerning the circumstances surrounding the unfortunate demise of Sahil. The details and circumstances leading up to the incident remain subject to investigation by the appropriate authorities,” the post read.The institute said the circumstances surrounding Wakode's death remained under investigation by legal and law enforcement agencies.“In view of the ongoing investigation, it was inappropriate to have set out or characterised details relating to the events preceding his demise before they had been duly established through the appropriate investigative process,” IIT Bombay stated in the post on X.Prof Doolla had allegedly caught Wakode using a mobile phone inside an examination hall on September 18. Hours later, the 20-year-old second-year student was found dead in his hostel room.Wakode’s parents have alleged that their son had complained of being subjected to casteist remarks a few days before his death. The allegations have led to protests by students on the IIT Bombay campus.The city crime branch is investigating a case of alleged abetment to suicide in connection with Wakode’s death.Police have collected CCTV footage showing Wakode’s movements during the examination in which he was allegedly caught copying.According to investigators, footage from September 18 shows Wakode inside the examination hall between about 12.30pm and 12.45pm, as the semester examination was nearing its end.The footage allegedly shows him bending down and looking at a mobile phone kept in his pocket. Police are also examining an allegation that he was using ChatGPT to answer questions during the examination.The footage then shows the invigilator noticing Wakode’s movements and approaching him. The invigilator is seen taking his answer sheet and asking him to leave the examination hall.Wakode is then seen getting up, collecting his belongings and preparing to leave. He appears to hand something to the invigilator, who is not visible in that part of the footage.Police are examining Wakode’s movements and interactions after he left the examination hall as they try to establish what happened in the hours before his death.The crime branch on Wednesday recorded statements from three students who were reportedly close to Wakode.Prof Doolla’s statement has not yet been recorded. Investigators said they first wanted to collect available digital evidence and record statements from other witnesses before questioning him about the incident.Police are also examining allegations of discrimination or harassment in connection with Wakode’s death.The resurfaced email is being examined against the backdrop of the allegations made by Wakode’s parents. The investigation will determine whether any such allegations have a bearing on the circumstances surrounding his death.
Article Summary: Email sent by IIT Bombay professor Suryanarayana Doolla has resurfaced amid allegations of caste discrimination. In the email, prof Doolla cautioned students against asking fellow students about their admission categories, JEE (Advanced) ranks or GATE scores. He said such questions could reveal their caste or whether they belonged to a reserved category.

Article Title: Benedict Arnold was once trusted by George Washington before switching allegiance to Britain and dying in England in 1801; the Revolutionary War general’s crypt is now part of a kindergarten classroom
Article Text:
Benedict Arnold went from George Washington’s trusted general to British ally; his crypt is now part of a kindergarten classroom. (Photo: Wiki/St Mary's, Battersea)

From Washington’s trusted officer to British ally

Arnold left for England and never returned

His crypt is now part of a classroom

Benedict Arnold’s historic crypt in London now forms part of a kindergarten classroom, more than two centuries after his death. (Photo: St Mary's, Battersea)

$15,000 headstone installed more than 200 years after his death

Benedict Arnold, one of the most controversial figures of the American Revolutionary War, ended his life far removed from the country where he had once earned the trust of General George Washington.Arnold had already experienced considerable hardship before joining the Continental Army. A businessman before his military career, he lost his shipping business during the Revolutionary War and was wounded in combat twice. Yet his military achievements eventually saw him rise to the rank of major general and become a trusted officer under Washington.His final resting place, however, is an unusual one. Arnold was buried in the crypt of St. Mary’s Church in Battersea, England, in 1801. Today, that crypt forms part of the church's basement and is used by a private kindergarten program.Arnold's fortunes appeared to improve after British forces withdrew from Philadelphia. Washington appointed him military commander of the city, giving Arnold an opportunity to rebuild his personal life.A businessman at heart, Arnold began pursuing commercial interests in Philadelphia, although his business activities drew criticism from some at the time.The position nevertheless allowed him to enjoy a more comfortable lifestyle.Philadelphia also played an important role in Arnold's personal life. It was there that he met Peggy Shippen, whom he later married. Shippen sympathized with the British cause and was subsequently suspected of being a British spy, according to the Museum of the American Revolution.Historians continue to debate the extent to which Shippen influenced Arnold's decision to change allegiance. What is established is that Arnold eventually defected to the British side.Arnold's switch of allegiance transformed his place in American history. He left New York for England in 1781 and never returned to the United States.Although the British military took Arnold in, he did not achieve the same authority or success he had enjoyed while serving the American revolutionary cause. He nevertheless established a life in Britain with his family and was respected in some British circles.Arnold died in England on June 14, 1801, aged 60.He was buried in the crypt of St. Mary's Church in Battersea. His wife, Peggy, and later their daughter were also buried there.The crypt eventually became part of the church's basement. The space is now rented by a private kindergarten and serves as a classroom, as well as a meeting space when school is not in session.The setting offers an unusual final chapter for a man whose name remains deeply connected to the American Revolution and the concept of betrayal.A belated effort was eventually made to give Arnold a more visible historical memorial.In 2004, former Connecticut state senator Bill Stanley sought to honor Arnold, who was born in Norwich, Connecticut. Stanley paid $15,000 for a granite headstone bearing an epitaph acknowledging Arnold's complicated military history, according to Smithsonian Magazine.The inscription describes Arnold as a “Sometime General in the Army of George Washington” and adds that the two nations he served during their conflict had ultimately united in lasting friendship.
Article Summary: Benedict Arnold was one of the most controversial figures of the American Revolutionary War. He became a trusted officer under General George Washington. Arnold eventually defected to the British side and never returned to the United States. He was buried in the crypt of St. Mary’s Church in Battersea, England, in 1801. Today, that crypt is used by a private kindergarten program.

Article Title: Delhi shocker: 2 minors among 3 held after teenager stabbed ‘16 times’
Article Text:
A 17-year-old boy was murdered in Anand Parbat after an argument escalated over a minor collision.





NEW DELHI: Police have apprehended a youth and two minors who allegedly murdered a 17-year-old boy, stabbing him multiple times in central Delhi’s Anand Parbat, after they brushed past each other in a narrow lane Tuesday.The murdered boy’s brother said he was stabbed 16 times. Police said seven to eight stab wounds have been found on the teenager’s body. “My mother is in denial,” said 18-year-old Mayank Dhingra, the boy’s brother. "She keeps asking me, ‘where is my son? I hope he got a good bandage. When will he be discharged?’ How do I keep telling her he is no more?” he asked.The teenager, a resident of Anand Parbat, was found injured in Gali No. 16, Than Singh Road, Tuesday night. A constable and some people who were nearby rushed him to Jeevan Mala Hospital, where doctors declared him brought dead. Police got a call around 8.30pm.The boy’s cousin Hrithik said the family was informed while the teenager was in hospital. “The doctor told us he had been stabbed multiple times. We were shocked. How could someone do this? He was just a teenager,” he said.An FIR under Section 103(1) of BNS, which provides for punishment for murder, was registered at Anand Parbat police station Tuesday.DCP (central) Rohit Rajbir Singh said CCTV footage, technical surveillance and local information helped the cops identify the attackers.Tushar (19), of Anand Parbat, was arrested, while two juveniles, aged 17 and 15, were apprehended from the area within seven hours of the murder. Police also found the knife they had allegedly used on the boy. Investigators have also not found any history of enmity between the boy and the trio.The three attackers told police that they were walking through Gali No. 16 and the boy was coming from the opposite direction. They accidentally collided while passing each other, following which an argument broke out. Police said the altercation escalated and they allegedly stabbed the teenager and fled.At the mortuary, as Mayank waited for his brother’s body, he recounted the moments before and after the family came to know about the murder. He said he was returning home Tuesday evening, while his mother was in a nearby lane at his aunt’s house.When she was first told about the attack, the boy’s mum “ran from one place to another.” Mayank said: “She finally found out that my brother was at a hospital. We rushed there. He had been stabbed 16 times. My brother had no enmity with anyone.”Mayank said his brother had stepped out of the house after their grandmother asked him to bring her some household goods. He never came back.
Article Summary: A 17-year-old boy was murdered in Anand Parbat after an argument escalated over a minor collision. Police said seven to eight stab wounds have been found on the teenager’s body. Police have apprehended a youth and two minors who allegedly murdered the boy.

Article Title: Delhi Minor Rape Case: Delhi minor rape case: Neighbours claim accused ‘fought over petty issues’
Article Text:
(The victim's identity has not been revealed to protect her privacy as per Supreme court directives on cases related to sexual assault)





NEW DELHI: Residents of Sriniwaspuri Extension, where brothers Hemant Singh and Mukesh Singh- accused of raping a minor-lived, said they kept their distance from the two.The brothers were close, neighbours said, and would usually be seen together, usually exercising or lounging on the terrace."They would start a fight if anyone even stepped onto their part of the terrace," said a neighbour, who did not wish to be named, adding that Hemant claimed to be a lawyer and said even if someone complained against him, nothing would happen to him.Hemant and Mukesh, along with Asif, were arrested Tuesday for the gang rape of a 17-year-old girl in south Delhi's Aastha Kunj Park.Investigators said the two brothers were familiar with the park's layout and its dark spots as they used to play cricket there. This is where they met Asif three months ago, police said.Hemant's father, advocate J R Dhankar, told police that Mukesh is a BSc student and Hemant is a lawyer, a claim that cops are verifying. Dhankar has accused police of framing his sons."Police picked them up from their home in Sriniwaspuri early in the morning without informing us. Their statements were taken forcibly... They were at home all day and were not outside when the incident occurred," he said.Their house was locked Wednesday.Neighbours said they had never seen Hemant go to work or wear a lawyer's coat. One added that she felt uncomfortable in their presence because of the "hostility" in their interactions with neighbours.The third accused, Asif, had been working for more than 10 years in Okhla Sabzi Mandi along with his uncle. People who knew Asif remained tight-lipped, only saying he was polite in their interactions. According to police, Asif is married and has a teenage daughter.Based on the survivor's statement, Asif was identified and tracked down Tuesday. He was arrested following a brief exchange of fire, in which he sustained bullet injuries in his leg. The two brothers were then nabbed based on his description, said police.
Article Summary: Hemant and Mukesh Singh, along with Asif, were arrested Tuesday for the gang rape of a 17-year-old girl in south Delhi's Aastha Kunj Park. The brothers were close, neighbours said, and would usually be seen together, usually exercising or lounging on the terrace.

Article Title: ‘No high court bench, no vote’: Meerut bar calls boycott of BJP leaders
Article Text:
Posters carrying the slogan were displayed at court entrances and on lawyers’ vehicles.

(With inputs from Munish Kumar in Meerut)





MEERUT: Meerut Bar Association on Wednesday intensified its agitation for a permanent high court bench in western Uttar Pradesh, announcing a boycott of BJP leaders over their alleged lack of support for the long-pending demand.Lawyers abstained from judicial work and staged protests at the court premises, with advocates from 22 western UP districts extending support. Posters carrying the slogan “No Bench, No Vote” were displayed at court entrances and on lawyers’ vehicles.At a general body meeting on Tuesday, the association resolved to bar BJP-elected representatives and office-bearers from entering the court complex. It also decided to initiate the withdrawal of vakalatnamas (a written legal document that a client signs to authorise a lawyer or advocate to represent them in a court of law) filed by its members for serving and former BJP representatives in various courts, including MP-MLA courts.Meerut Bar Association president Anuj Kumar Sharma said the decisions followed a meeting between a nine-member delegation and chief minister Yogi Adityanath “We have been pursuing the demand for HC bench for decades. People from this region have to travel to Prayagraj for justice, which involves considerable time and expense. If the govt says it cannot provide a bench, the responsibility cannot simply be shifted elsewhere. We will intensify our democratic and legal struggle until the demand is addressed,” Sharma said.He said the delegation submitted a memorandum to the CM, who told them govt could not provide a bench and advised them to approach Supreme Court. Sharma also alleged that the lawyers were asked to hand over their mobile phones and were not allowed to photograph the meeting.The association also decided to withdraw the vakalatnama of Rajya Sabha MP Laxmikant Vajpayee in connection with the demand and seek early termination of the membership of BJP-linked elected representatives associated with it.Central Struggle Committee is likely to meet in Saharanpur. Lawyers also plan to approach traders and other city associations to mobilise wider public support. The move has sparked dissent among lawyers, with BJP-supporting advocates opposing the proposed boycott and withdrawal of vakalatnamas.
Article Summary: Lawyers abstained from judicial work and staged protests at the court premises. Posters carrying the slogan ‘No Bench, No Vote’ were displayed at court entrances and on lawyers’ vehicles. At a general body meeting, the association resolved to bar BJP-elected representatives and office-bearers from entering the court complex.

Article Title: Surinder Koli’s post-mortem report is out: Police confirm suicide, rule out murder
Article Text:
Surender Koli was confirmed to have died from ante-mortem hanging according to the post-mortem examination





DEHRADUN: The post-mortem examination of former Nithari case accused Surender Koli has confirmed “ante-mortem hanging”, indicating that he was alive when he hanged himself, police said on Wednesday, ruling out the possibility that he was killed first and then suspended.A ligature mark was found around Koli’s neck, while doctors also noted saliva dribbling, a fracture of the hyoid bone and petechiae, with bleeding from the nose and mouth consistent with hanging, police said.Investigators reviewing CCTV footage from around the time of his death did not find any suspicious activity.Koli was seen walking outside his tea kiosk at around 8pm in an apparently worried state, after which police are now investigating what may have led to his death.Kotwali Nagar SHO Kundan Singh Rana told TOI, “Surender Koli’s death was a case of suicide. The postmortem report states ‘ante-mortem hanging,’ indicating that he was alive at the time of hanging. However, the reason behind Koli’s suicide is still being investigated. Police are gathering information from people based on the analysis of his Call Detail Records (CDR).”Police are examining Koli’s Call Detail Records as part of the probe and are speaking to people who were in contact with him before his death.Koli, 50, was found dead inside a tea kiosk he had opened in Haridwar around 10 days before his death. Passersby alerted the police after spotting him hanging from a noose.A forensic team examined the spot and collected evidence. No suicide note was found.Koli’s death had initially raised questions after social activist Narayan Singh Rawat claimed he suspected murder.Rawat told TOI that he had helped Koli with Rs 25,000 to set up the tea kiosk and alleged that Koli had complained to him about harassment by a local farmer leader over an alleged outstanding amount of around Rs 5,000.However, Koli’s younger brother Anand had told TOI that he remained in regular contact with him and that Koli had never discussed any issue that was troubling him.Anand said Koli had spoken about starting his own business and had been making plans for his livelihood.Koli, who was arrested in the infamous Nithari killings case, was acquitted in the final case by the Supreme Court last November after spending nearly two decades in jail.He had subsequently moved to Haridwar, where he initially worked as a security guard before starting the tea kiosk.
Article Summary: Surender Koli, 50, was found dead inside a tea kiosk he had opened in Haridwar around 10 days before his death. The postmortem report states ‘ante-mortem hanging,’ indicating that he was alive at the time of hanging. No suicide note was found.

Article Title: 'Threatened with acid attack': Delhi woman drugged, raped on pretext of job offer
Article Text:
The accused claimed to have contacts in the police and threatened to throw acid on the woman if she reported the incident (AI Image)
